attractions.name: Qissa Khwani Bazaar
attractions.description: The historic 'Storytellers' Market', a centuries-old bazaar known for its atmosphere, dry fruits, and traditional shops.

attractions.name: Bala Hisar Fort
attractions.description: A centuries-old fort overlooking the city, historically used as a military garrison, offering views of Peshawar.

attractions.name: Peshawar Museum
attractions.description: One of the best museums in Pakistan for Gandhara-era Buddhist art and artifacts, housed in a colonial-era building.

attractions.name: Chowk Yadgar
attractions.description: A historic central square and monument in the old city, surrounded by markets and street food stalls.

attractions.name: Sethi House / Sethi Mohalla
attractions.description: Beautifully restored 19th-century merchant houses showcasing traditional Peshawari architecture and woodwork.

food_places.name: Namak Mandi
food_places.specialty: Famous open-air tikka and karahi street food area

food_places.name: Charsi Tikka (Namak Mandi)
food_places.specialty: One of the most well-known tikka spots in Pakistan

food_places.name: Qehwa Khana (tea houses, Old City)
food_places.specialty: Traditional green tea (qehwa) and local snacks

transportation.notes: Fast route via the M-1 Motorway
Scenic but longer option compared to bus/flight
Convenient for reaching the old city and cantonment areas
Budget-friendly along the main BRT corridor

weather_info.climate_type: Semi-arid, continental climate with hot summers and cool winters

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Cool, 5-18°C, occasional light fog in the mornings
Some rainfall, generally lighter than in Punjab/Sindh

travel_tips.tip: Use the Ring Road to bypass the congested city center when traveling between the cantonment area and University Town.
Ride-hailing apps are generally more predictable for tourists than negotiating with local rickshaws in unfamiliar areas.
Check current local security advisories before planning day trips outside the city, as conditions can change; stick to well-known tourist areas.
Visit Qissa Khwani Bazaar and Namak Mandi in the early evening when the food stalls and shops are liveliest.

history.founded: One of the oldest cities in South Asia, with a history spanning over 2,000 years
history.city_history: Peshawar was a major center of the ancient Gandhara civilization and an important stop on trade routes connecting South and Central Asia. It has been ruled by the Persians, Greeks, Kushans, Mughals, Sikhs, and the British, and its old city and bazaars still reflect this long, layered history.
history.province_history: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has historically been a crossroads between South and Central Asia, home to the ancient Gandhara civilization, and later part of the Mughal Empire, Sikh Empire, and British India, before joining Pakistan in 1947. It was renamed from the North-West Frontier Province to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2010.
